passages.notes: Read visually in the page renditions for leaves n53-n56. The Ordinary ends mid-page: a thick-and-thin double rule runs across the full measure below Deo gratias on p. xlvi, and the rest of that page is blank. Corrected on 2026-07-31: this record said what follows the rule is a devotional appendix "headed as versicles and a prayer for the sovereign". It is not, and nothing follows the rule on p. xlvi at all. The next leaf, n57, is printed p. xlvii and is headed BEFORE, AND AT THE BENEDICTION, carrying O salutaris hostia and Tantum ergo in the same facing columns - Benediction of the Blessed Sacrament, not a prayer for the sovereign. That leaf was rendered and read to settle the point. Two consequences worth recording: the boundary of the Ordinary is the rule and not the end of a page, and the book's roman pagination does not stop at xlvi as this edition's own notes imply, but continues at least to xlvii.

work.author: Catholic Church, in an anonymous English translation published by Eugene Cummiskey, Philadelphia
work.description: A nineteenth-century English lay hand missal giving the Masses of the Roman Missal for the use of the laity, with the orations printed in English only and the chant propers in facing Latin and English columns. The translation is anonymous; the title matter records publication with the approbation of the Bishop of Philadelphia. It is a devotional companion to the Latin altar book, not an official liturgical translation, and its rubrics, commemorations, and Holy Week material are those in force before the 1955 and 1960 reforms.
